verdict.rationale: Trello's REST API docs describe generating an API key and a delegated authorization flow (the `1/authorize` route or OAuth1.0) that issues user tokens whose scope of permissions and length of access are configurable via query params, so an agent can get a limited, expiring token. An OAuth 2.0 API client is also listed. Missing for 10: any detail on how fine-grained the scopes are (e.g., per-board or per-workspace restriction, read-only vs write breakdown), any agent- or service-account-specific credential guidance, and independent or hands-on corroboration that least-privilege tokens work in practice.
